contentChunks.htmlValue: Availability & resources
M3 Expressive update

May 2025

Buttons now have a wider variety of shapes and sizes, toggle functionality, and can change shape when selected. More on M3 Expressive

Variants and naming:

  • Default and toggle (selection)

  • Color styles are now configurations (elevated, filled, tonal, outlined, text)

Shapes: 

  • Round and square

  • Shape morphs when pressed

  • Shape morphs when selected

Sizes:

  • Extra small

  • Small (existing, default)

  • Medium

  • Large

  • Extra large

New padding for small buttons:

  • 16dp (recommended to match padding of new sizes)

  • 24dp (no longer recommended)

contentChunks.htmlValue: Differences from M2

• Color: New color mappings and compatibility with dynamic color. Icons and labels now share the same color. Neutral text button is no longer recommended.

  • Icons: Standard size for leading and trailing icons is now 20dp

  • Shape: Fully-rounded corner radius and additional height options

contentChunks.htmlValue: Color

Color values are implemented through design tokens. For designers, this means working with color values that correspond with tokens. In implementation, a color value will be a token that references a value.

  • There are five built-in button color styles: elevated, filled, tonal, outlined, and text

  • The default and toggle buttons use different colors

  • Toggle buttons don’t use the text style

star

These color roles were chosen to create design coherence and familiarity. Other color roles can be used as long as the container and text have a 3:1 contrast ratio. For example, tertiary and on tertiary.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Buttons communicate actions that people can take. They are typically placed throughout the UI, in places like:

  • Dialogs

  • Modal windows

  • Forms

  • Cards

  • Toolbars

They can also be placed within standard button groups.

contentChunks.footer: Use visually-prominent filled buttons for the most important actions
contentChunks.altText: Video call app with prominent filled button to join and end a call.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Buttons are just one option for representing actions in a product and shouldn’t be overused. Too many buttons on a screen can disrupt the visual hierarchy.

Consider placing additional actions in a navigation rail, set of chips, text links, or icon buttons.

contentChunks.footer: Use buttons for discrete actions
contentChunks.altText: 1 button placed on bottom right of screen.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t clutter your UI with too many buttons. Consider presenting low-priority actions in overflow menus or as icon buttons.
contentChunks.altText: 3 buttons side by side on bottom of screen.

contentChunks.footer: A button container’s width is dynamically set to fit its label text
contentChunks.altText: Filled button on menu screen.

contentChunks.footer: Button container width can be responsive, which allows it to stretch horizontally
contentChunks.altText: Filled button as wide as layout grid.

contentChunks.footer: A button container’s width shouldn’t be narrower than its label text
contentChunks.altText: Filled button with label text overflowing the container.

  1. Elevated button

contentChunks.htmlValue:
A button group is a collection of buttons that relate to each other and can respond to one another. Both buttons and icon buttons can be used inside a button group.

In some cases, there are primary and secondary actions within a button group. Buttons with primary actions should have a higher visual emphasis through size, color, or shape.

More on button groups

contentChunks.footer: Different sized buttons in a button group help emphasize the main action from secondary actions
contentChunks.altText: Audio app with play, next, and back buttons.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Toggle buttons

Toggle buttons should be used for binary selections, such as Save or Favorite. When toggle buttons are pressed, they can change color, shape, and labels.

Toggle buttons should use an outlined icon when unselected, and a filled version of the icon when selected. If a filled version doesn’t exist, increase the weight instead.

By default, toggle buttons change from round to square when selected.

contentChunks.footer: Use toggle buttons for binary actions
contentChunks.altText: Toggle “stop” button in timer app.

contentChunks.htmlValue: If the label changes on selected or unselected states, be mindful of the character count. Changing the label significantly is disruptive to the user and the page layout.

contentChunks.footer: When using toggleable buttons, keep the label character count a similar length for both states
contentChunks.altText: Toggleable “start” and “reset” buttons.

contentChunks.footer: The label length shouldn’t change dramatically to be longer or shorter
contentChunks.altText: Toggleable “start” and “reset back to beginning” buttons.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Label text

Label text is the most important element of a button. It describes the action that will occur if someone taps a button. It should be very brief, ideally 1–3 words.

Use sentence case, which only capitalizes the first word and proper nouns. This allows the text to distinguish proper nouns, for example: Book with Flights, not BOOK WITH FLIGHTS.

Don’t truncate or wrap label text. It should always be fully visible on a single line.

contentChunks.footer: Use sentence case for button label text, capitalizing the first word and proper nouns
contentChunks.altText: Button with label text “See all recipes.”

contentChunks.footer: Don’t wrap text. For maximum legibility, label text should remain on a single line.
contentChunks.altText: Button with wrapped label.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Buttons with the outlined and text color style depend on the colors to be recognizable from other text and elements. Use caution when putting these buttons next to visually similar elements, such as chips or large text.

contentChunks.footer: The outlined button style is very similar to chips. Consider using a filled or tonal button instead.
contentChunks.altText: Chips next to an outlined button, highlighting their similarities.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Container

Button containers hold the label text and optional icon. Buttons with the text color style have a visible container only when hovered, focused, or pressed.

Buttons with a round shape have containers with fully rounded corners.

contentChunks.footer: Round buttons have containers with fully rounded corners
contentChunks.altText: Round button.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Buttons with a square shape have containers with more subtle rounding that changes based on button size.

contentChunks.footer: Square buttons have square containers and change radius as the button size changes
contentChunks.altText: Square buttons with different radii.

contentChunks.footer: A button’s width dynamically adjusts to the label text
contentChunks.altText: Button with the label text “Edit playlist” within the container.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid setting a fixed width smaller than the label text
contentChunks.altText: Button with text larger than its container.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Icon (optional)

Icons visually communicate the button’s action and help draw attention. They should be placed on the leading side of the button, before the label text.

contentChunks.footer: Place the icon to the left of the label in buttons with text in left-to-right languages
contentChunks.altText: Filled button with the icon to the left of the label in a left-to-right language.

contentChunks.footer: Place the icon to the right of the label in buttons with text in right-to-left languages
contentChunks.altText: Filled button with the icon to the right of the label in a right-to-left language.

contentChunks.footer: Use icons that clearly communicate their meaning
contentChunks.altText: Button with shopping cart icon and text label “Add to cart”.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t vertically align an icon and text in the center of a button
contentChunks.altText: Button with Plus icon vertically above the text label “Add to watch list”.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use two icons in the same button
contentChunks.altText: Button with two icons.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Color styles
Elevated style

The elevated button style is the same as the tonal button, but with a shadow. 

To avoid overusing shadows, use the elevated style only when absolutely necessary, such as when the button requires visual separation from a visually prominent background.

contentChunks.footer: Elevated buttons provide separation from a visually prominent background
contentChunks.altText: Elevated button on a scrim background.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Buttons at higher elevations typically have more emphasis in a design, and should be used sparingly. For high emphasis, consider the filled style instead.

contentChunks.footer: Higher elevation increases the emphasis of a button
contentChunks.altText: Elevated button in a shopping experience.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Filled style
The filled button style has the most visual impact after the FAB, and should be used for important, final actions that complete a flow, like Save, Join now, or Confirm.

contentChunks.footer: Filled buttons have high visual impact when used for important actions
contentChunks.altText: Filled button reading “Make payment.”

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Since they have such strong emphasis, the filled style should be used sparingly, ideally for only one action on a page.

In some cases, filled buttons can use tertiary colors.

contentChunks.footer: Filled buttons can be responsive to the layout grid and help emphasize main actions
contentChunks.altText: Filled “pause” button in a music app.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Tonal style

The tonal button style is useful in contexts where a lower-priority button requires slightly more emphasis than an outline would give, such as Next in an onboarding flow. Tonal buttons use the secondary color mapping.

contentChunks.footer: The tonal style has less emphasis than filled or emphasis
contentChunks.altText: Shopping app with 2 tonal-style filled buttons.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Outlined style

The outlined style is ideal for medium-emphasis buttons which contain actions that are important, but aren’t the primary action in a product.

Outlined buttons pair well with filled buttons to indicate alternative, secondary actions.

contentChunks.footer: Outlined buttons contain less important supporting actions
contentChunks.altText: Outlined buttons for less important actions, including a back button and a button that reads “Next movie.”

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Outlined buttons display a stroke around the button container, and have no fill by default. 

They should be placed on simple backgrounds, not visually prominent backgrounds such as images or videos.

contentChunks.footer: Outlined buttons display a stroke around the button container
contentChunks.altText: Outlined button for “add to cart” in shopping app.

contentChunks.footer: Outlined buttons can be used on backgrounds with a color gradient
contentChunks.altText: Outlined button labeled Add to calendar on a pink/purple background.

contentChunks.footer: Use caution when placing outlined buttons on top of images. Customizing the button to have a contrasting container fill can help ensure legibility of label text. Or, use a filled button instead.
contentChunks.altText: 2 photos, each with an outlined button with a custom fill.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Text style

The text button style should be used for the lowest priority actions, especially when presenting multiple options.

They should be placed on simple backgrounds, not visually prominent backgrounds such as images or videos. The container isn’t visible until someone interacts with the button.

Don’t underline the text button. Use hyperlinked body text instead to emphasize links. More on hyperlinks

contentChunks.footer: Use text buttons for the lowest priority actions
contentChunks.altText: Example calendar screen with 2 text buttons and 1 split button.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Text buttons are often placed within components such as cards, dialogs, and snackbars. Since text buttons don’t have a visible container in their default state, they don’t distract from nearby content.

However, since there’s no container, the label text color must always be recognizable from non-button text and elements.

contentChunks.footer: Text button in a snackbar
contentChunks.altText: Text button labeled “Retry” in a snackbar.

contentChunks.footer: Text button against an image background
contentChunks.altText: Text button labeled “View album” on an album cover background.

contentChunks.htmlValue: In cards, text buttons help maintain an emphasis on card content.

contentChunks.footer: Text button in a card
contentChunks.altText: Text button labeled “Learn more” in an information card about sourdough bread.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Dialogs use text buttons because the absence of a container helps unify the action with the dialog text.

Align text buttons to the trailing edge of dialogs, on the right for left-to-right languages and on the left for right-to-left languages.

contentChunks.footer: Text buttons in a dialog
contentChunks.altText: Modal dialog with the title “Subscribe to our newsletter?” and trailing buttons “Cancel” and “Subscribe”.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Adaptive design
Resizing
When scaling layouts for large screen devices, buttons can adapt their visual presentation, size, alignment, and arrangement to fit different contexts and user needs.
Choose the best button position based on screen size.

contentChunks.footer: Filled buttons are end-aligned below flight information in a compact window
contentChunks.altText: Flights app in compact screen with buttons below flight information.

contentChunks.footer: Filled buttons are start-aligned beside flight information in a large window
contentChunks.altText: Flights app in large screen with buttons to the left of flight information.

contentChunks.htmlValue: The icon and label text in a button stay centered and grouped as the button's width changes.

contentChunks.footer: Keep the icon and label text grouped and centered
contentChunks.altText: 2 buttons with horizontally centered text labels.

contentChunks.footer: Don't ungroup the icon and label text or let them anchor to opposite sides of the button
contentChunks.altText: 1 button with centered text label, 1 button with icon and label aligned to opposite edges.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Buttons can be customized to change size and scaling behavior across different breakpoints. 

To avoid creating very long buttons in large windows, constrain button width or place buttons beside other elements.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t allow the button to stretch in a way that creates long, flat buttons with very little content inside
contentChunks.altText: Button width is over-stretched with screen width.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Presentation

The size and placement of buttons can change as parent containers, such as cards, adapt for larger screens. 

Keep items, including buttons, in the same order between large and small screens to provide a consistent experience for screen readers and keyboard navigation.

contentChunks.footer: Buttons can move in the layout, but elements should remain in the same order
contentChunks.altText: 2 buttons scaling to accommodate different device sizes.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Use cases

People should be able to do the following with assistive technology: 

  • Use a button to perform an action
  • Navigate to and activate a button
Interaction & style

Color contrast

Enabled buttons need a 3:1 contrast ratio with the background to meet accessibility best practices. 

This is measured from the container for elevated, filled, and tonal button styles, and the label text for outlined and text button styles.

contentChunks.footer: Higher contrast helps differentiate elements
contentChunks.altText: Diagram of color contrast ratios for buttons.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
200% text size

Avoid excessive text wrapping or truncation by choosing concise strings. 

On Android, button labels should be kept concise enough to fit within two lines after the text size is increased to 200%. If a button label exceeds this limit and gets truncated, provide an alternative way to access the full content in a single tap.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid excessive text wrapping or truncation by choosing concise strings
contentChunks.altText: 200% text size on a mobile screen. The overly long button text wraps to a second line: “Download playlist for offline access”.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Rapid clicks

On the web, you can use a modified motion curve to avoid resonant effects from overlapping animations. This provides a smoother experience for interactions where you anticipate multiple clicks or taps in succession.

contentChunks.footer: Use the modified motion curve if rapid click or pointer interactions are expected
contentChunks.altText: A media player where the “next track” button is clicked rapidly, and is transformed with a smooth motion effect.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Keyboard navigation

KeysActions
TabNavigate to a button
Space or EnterActivate a button
Labeling elements

The accessibility label for a button should match the visible label text on the button such as Done, Send, or Reply. 

It can contain extra contextual information if necessary.

contentChunks.altText: Accessibility tags for a text-only button.
